result.rationale: The diff lowercases blacklist entries (`process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(",").map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) but compares with raw `guest` in `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, and the attendee dedupe uses exact `guest === attendee.email` with no case normalization on either side. A mixed-case duplicate email therefore passes both checks and is inserted via `createMany`, creating a duplicate Attendee row and double invitation; a blacklisted mixed-case email slips through. This is a verifiable correctness defect introduced by the new handler.

judged_text: Email canonicalization is inconsistent across this path: the blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is compared raw (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), and the existing-attendee dedupe (`guest === attendee.email`) is case-sensitive against emails stored verbatim. An attendee entered as "User@X.com" when "user@x.com" already exists on the booking passes the dedupe and is inserted as a second Attendee row for the same person (and the same person is invited twice); conversely a mixed-case guest matching a lowercased blacklist entry is not filtered. There is no single canonical form enforced at write or comparison time.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, blacklist entries are normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but each incoming `guest` is compared without canonicalization (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). The existing-attendee dedupe is also case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email`). Since neither server schema (`z.string().email()`) nor handler lowercases/normalizes emails before comparing/writing, mixed-case variants can bypass both the blacklist and the dedupe and be inserted as additional attendee rows, resulting in duplicate invites.
